input: Our team holds meetings about how to hold fewer meetings.

response.answer:
The Perpetual Agenda Loop (fictional)

Fictional patent sketch.

FIGURE 1
```text
[A: rotating agenda wheel — spins through topics]
                   ↓
[B: consensus-seeking rubber stamp — applies 'approved' to minutes]
                   ↓
[C: coffee-stained notepad — records action items as vague suggestions]
BACK TO A: the vague suggestions become new agenda topics
```

CLAIM 1 — An apparatus for transforming productive time into discussions about productivity, while ensuring that the original problem remains perpetually on the agenda.

BENCH TEST — In this imagined conference room, the rotating agenda wheel lands on "Streamlining Communication." The consensus-seeking stamp dutifully marks the minutes as "approved." The coffee-stained notepad captures "explore synergy" as a key action item. This vague suggestion then cycles back to the agenda wheel, ready for another meeting about how to streamline communication.

REMOVE ONE PART
A: Lose the rotating agenda wheel; the meeting would have a fixed topic, but might get stuck on one issue.
B: Lose the consensus-seeking stamp; decisions would be less official, but might actually be made.
C: Lose the coffee-stained notepad; action items would be clearer, but might be too concrete to avoid.

Try outside the sketch: before the next meeting, write down one specific, actionable task for yourself related to meeting efficiency.

Choose a part and paste this sketch to request a revision.
